findings.title: Google Meet booking with no destination calendar throws TypeError
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` gives `undefined` when the array is empty or null. handleNewBooking sets it to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067). The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. So any booking whose location is Google Meet and that has no destination calendar now crashes in `EventManager.create`. Before this change it fell back to Cal Video, which is the purpose of this branch. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video references no longer store credentialId, so cancelling leaves the meeting in place
findings.body: The old code stored `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results, i.e. video meetings: `createMeeting` sets `credentialId: credential.id` (videoClient.ts:78). The new code is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so every new `_video` booking reference is saved without a credentialId. handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set (handleCancelBooking.ts:491-501). As a result, cancelling a new Zoom, Daily or other video booking silently leaves the meeting on the provider. Keep `result.credentialId` for both cases.

findings.title: Org slug condition inverted
findings.body: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, and the same happened to `requestedSlug` on line 153. This is not a type-only refactor: the logic is reversed. With billing disabled (self-hosted), organizations are now created with no slug. With billing enabled, the slug is claimed straight away instead of being kept as `requestedSlug` until payment. Restore `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` and `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {}`.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback can never match
findings.body: This branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but it then searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, i.e. for a calendar whose externalId is null or empty. That never matches, so the result is `undefined`. The old fallback used the destination calendar's externalId. For references with no stored `externalCalendarId`, which includes older bookings, `events.update` is now called with `calendarId: undefined` and fails. `deleteEvent` (line 317) falls back to "primary" and gets a 404, which it resolves silently (line 335), so the event stays on the non-primary calendar. Fall back to the main host's destination calendar as before, for example `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

findings.title: Destination calendars without credentialId now write to primary
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` is found only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. EventManager still supports destination calendars without a credentialId: it creates the event on every credential of that integration (EventManager.ts:375-381). For those, the lookup finds nothing and the event goes to "primary" instead of `destination.externalId` as before. Pass the destination's externalId (CalendarManager.createEvent already receives it as `externalId`), or fall back to matching by integration.

findings.title: Team members' calendars dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (lines 1063-1067). In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing, and the collective hosts' destination calendars collected at line 993 are thrown away. This is the scenario the PR sets out to fix. Start from `[]` for collective events, e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

findings.title: Recurring cancel branch now runs once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring branch is now inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Each pass deletes every updated booking's first calendar reference using all of the organizer's calendar credentials. With N references (one per collective host), the same deletes run N times, while team members' events for the remaining occurrences are never deleted because only `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` are used. Consider moving the recurring handling out of the loop and iterating over each updated booking's references with their own credentials.

findings.title: Merging on reschedule deletes only the first old calendar event
findings.body: Updating now goes through every calendar reference, but the old-booking cleanup still uses `booking.references.find(...)`. For a collective booking with several hosts' references, only the first old event is deleted, and the other hosts keep a stale event.

findings.title: Error in updateAllCalendarEvents is now swallowed
findings.body: `message` is still built but `console.error(message)` was removed, so a failed update produces no log entry, only `success: false` results. Keep the log line.

findings.title: loadUsers turns validation errors into a generic 500
findings.body: The new `Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is not an HttpError, so the catch block rethrows it as a 500 "Unable to load users" rather than a 400. Also, `return users.length ? users : eventType.users` dropped the old `|| []` fallback.

contracts.action: createAllCalendarEvents creates one event per destination calendar, fetching missing credentials from DB
contracts.before_after: Before: one createEvent with the organizer credential. After: one per destination; external credentials loaded via prisma with app slug; result carries externalId/credentialId for references.
contracts.visible_effect: Booking references saved in handleNewBooking from referencesToCreate (EventManager.ts:163-171); attendees see events in each host calendar.
contracts.failure_mode: createEvent errors are caught in CalendarManager and returned as success:false; credential missing in DB silently skips that host. Video references lose credentialId (finding).

contracts.action: Google update/delete fall back when no externalCalendarId
contracts.before_after: Before: used destination calendar id; after: lookup on falsy id always undefined
contracts.visible_effect: Reschedule fails or cancel leaves event on calendar
Org without slug (no billing) or slug claimed before payment

summary: The PR turns destinationCalendar into an array so collective events land in every host's calendar. It introduces two merge blockers. EventManager.create throws when the location is Google Meet and there is no destination calendar. The org-creation slug condition is inverted. It also has several regressions: video references lose their credentialId, so cancelling no longer deletes the meeting; Google update/delete fall back to a lookup that never matches; and team calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar.
